external_entities.name: Duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who uses the dispatch console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state how an engineer signs in.

external_entities.name: Scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: Dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript app opened by duty engineers and used to call the dispatch API and receive live job status.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app and our corporate web host serves it.
processes.notes: The console and API are served from different origins. CORS configuration, including allowed origins and credential support, was not recorded.

processes.name: Dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer; it reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
processes.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

processes.name: Schedule importer
processes.description: A process that pulls the scheduling partner's SOAP feed, parses XML documents, archives them, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The importer presents an API token when posting to the dispatch API. The token was issued when the importer was built and has not been rotated.

data_stores.name: Dispatch database
data_stores.description: The database containing job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order carries the token or session that created it, and nothing about the person behind that token.

data_stores.name: Schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder on the corporate file store containing each document downloaded by the schedule importer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The console and API are served from different origins, so the API answers the console cross-origin. CORS allowed origins and credential support were not recorded.

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and holds a WebSocket to the dispatch API for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: It was not recorded whether the socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the engineer's session again after opening.

data_flows.name: read and write dispatch data
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order

data_flows.name: publish planned work
data_flows.description: The scheduling partner publishes tomorrow's planned work to the schedule importer through its SOAP feed.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.
data_flows.notes: Nothing was written down about how the partner identifies the importer or how the importer identifies the partner.

data_flows.name: write schedule archive
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded XML document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: The importer presents an API token. That token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The network where duty engineers sit and the schedule importer runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: Production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company zone holding the live estate, with authority to move a crew and change the work a depot does that day.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: A corporate laptop holds none of the control-plane rights. The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: Scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the separate company that publishes planned work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API presents a web interface because the description refers to cross-origin responses and CORS configuration.
assumptions.basis: The console and API are served from different origins, and the API's cross-origin behavior is configured with CORS.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database has confidential data because it contains crew mobile numbers and credentials in the form of tokens or sessions.
assumptions.basis: The database holds crew mobile numbers and each job order carries the token or session that created it.
